passage:
"Hold my hand, Karthik. Look, the light is red."
"Red means stop!"
"That's right, even for us," said Sabina, halting at the kerb. "Cars are big and cannot stop quickly."
"Why are you waiting, Mummy?"
"Because I follow the rule too."
A man hurried across in front of them. "He did not wait!" Karthik said.
"No. We wait, because the rule keeps us safe."
The little green man lit up. "Now?"
"Look left, look right first."
They crossed together, and Karthik puffed out his chest. "I stopped at the red!"

qa.q: What did Karthik say red means?
How does Karthik feel after crossing?
qa.a: He feels proud: he puffs out his chest and announces that he stopped at the red.

qa.q: What helped Karthik understand the rule?
qa.a: Sabina explained in simple words that cars cannot stop quickly and followed the rule herself even when someone else did not.

qa.q: How might Sabina see the man crossing against the light?
qa.a: Sabina probably sees it as unsafe and a poor example for Karthik, so she tells him they wait because the rule keeps them safe.

grounding: A child holds a parent's hand at a red light, feels proud following the rule, and the parent explains simply and models it.

passage:
From Simran, Jeevan's mother, in the class safety diary.
This week we walked to school instead of taking the bus. At the big crossing, Jeevan grabbed my hand before I even asked. When the man turned red, he pulled me back. "Red means stop, Mumma!" I explained, "The cars go fast. They can't stop quickly, so we wait." One morning the road was empty and I wanted to rush, but I waited anyway because he was watching. At the gate he told his teacher, "I stopped at red. I'm a good walker." He looked so proud.

qa.q: What did Jeevan say when the man turned red?
How did Jeevan feel when he told his teacher he stopped at red?
qa.a: He felt proud of following the rule and being a good walker.

qa.q: What did Simran do that helps a child respect safety rules?
qa.a: She explained simply why cars can't stop quickly and followed the rule herself even when the road was empty.

qa.q: How might Jeevan's teacher feel hearing his news?
qa.a: The teacher likely feels pleased and wants to praise his careful crossing. 😊

grounding: A young boy holds his mother's hand and stops at the red light, feels proud, and his mother explains why and models the rule.

passage: The road by the bus stand in the kasba was full of tractors, buses and bicycles. Pranav held Papa's hand tight. A boy on a cycle zipped across without looking, and a bus honked loudly. Pranav jumped. "Why did he go?" Papa, Naveen, shook his head. "He was in a hurry. But buses are big and can't stop fast. So we wait till it's clear, even when we're late." They waited. Papa looked left, right, left, out loud. Pranav copied him. When they crossed, Pranav held Papa's hand the whole way and grinned. "We did it right, Papa!"

qa.q: How did Pranav feel after they crossed?
qa.a: He felt proud and happy that they had crossed the right way, grinning at Papa.

qa.q: How did Naveen teach the rule, not just tell it?
qa.a: He explained simply why buses can't stop fast and looked left, right, left out loud so Pranav could copy him.

qa.q: How might Naveen feel when Pranav says "We did it right, Papa!"?
qa.a: He probably feels proud and relieved that his son is learning to be careful.

grounding: A young boy holds his father's hand and waits to cross a busy road, feeling proud, as his father explains why and models the rule.
